header:
Date: 2026-03-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (SummitCloud - Head of ML Platform), Roberto Diaz (SummitCloud - CTO), Mina Patel (SummitCloud - Procurement)
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in; customer evaluating capacity upgrade and expansion to EU and APAC regions. Discussion covered dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, committed contract extension for 12 months with discounted rates, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and a follow-up benchmark run on Redwood Dedicated. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark plan, and contract alignment.
topics: Capacity upgrade (add 2x dedicated GPU pools); additional regions (eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1); contract extension (12-month committed); security/compliance (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs); benchmarks and SLA targets (p95/p99 latency); procurement timeline and PO process.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll start in a sec. from Redwood side it's me Lena and Marcus, thanks for making the time.
[00:15] Aisha Khan: Hi thanks, happy to be here. we wanted to go over renewal and the expansion asks. we've seen steady growth and want to lock capacity for q2.
[00:30] Marcus Chen: Great. quick agenda: capacity options, multi-region routing, security checklist, and pricing/contract. anything to add?
[00:40] Roberto Diaz: Procurement stuff at the end, timeline. Mina is on the call to confirm PO steps.
[00:45] Mina Patel: yep thanks.
[01:05] Lena Park: Cool. Aisha, can you remind us of current usage profile? what percentiles, burst patterns?
[01:15] Aisha Khan: Sure. right now we're on hosted API for most traffic, about 600k tokens/day, spikes to 1.1M during promotions, p95 latency around 320ms on default redwood-infer (notes: sometimes called 'Redwood Infer' in logs). Our biggest pain is the weekends when seq length increases and latency variability hits p99.
[01:45] Marcus Chen: That aligns with what we saw. For predictable throughput and lower unit cost we recommended Dedicated, you're already familiar but quick recap: dedicated GPU pools give reserved capacity, predictable tail latencies and can be pinned to region.
[02:05] Aisha Khan: We're considering 2x the current committed capacity, plus wanting eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 for latency to EU and APAC customers. What are the options?
[02:20] Lena Park: You can add dedicated pools in those regions. There are two paths: a) multi-region dedicated pools (recommended) with routing policy so traffic goes to nearest region, or b) keep hosted in new regions which is faster to stand up but less predictable on tail SLAs. Tradeoffs are latency predictability and cost.
[02:40] Roberto Diaz: What's the cost delta roughly for dedicated per region? and any network egress we should plan for?
[02:50] Lena Park: Quick rough: adding a dedicated pool in a region adds a base monthly commit — we'll share exact numbers but expect about 20-30% extra over a single-region commit depending on GPU type and utilization. Egress is charged at cloud rates, and we'll include estimates.
[03:15] Aisha Khan: Okay. On security we need SOC 2 type 2 evidence, KMS integration, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also SSO/SAML.
[03:30] Marcus Chen: All supported. Redwood Private offers VPC connector or full private deployments if you need air-gapped. For hosted/dedicated we have customer-managed KMS integrations and detailed audit logs; we'll send the SOC2 pack. Note: our SOC2 doc is in the security repo, I'll attach link after.
[03:55] Mina Patel: Procurement question: if we do a 12-month committed extension with additional regions, do we sign an amendment or a new contract? timeline to get a PO?
[04:10] Lena Park: Typically we do an amendment to the existing agreement for dedicated capacity add-ons; legal can fast-track. we can support PO and invoice terms, net30 standard. We'll confirm in the quote.
[04:30] Aisha Khan: Any concerns about model variants falling back to hosted if dedicated capacity hits limits? we need graceful degradation.
[04:40] Marcus Chen: Yes, we have smart routing and automatic fallback policies: requests can fall back to a compatible hosted variant. We'll configure per-route fallback rules, and you can set an allowance for overflow so critical endpoints never see errors, just slightly higher latency.
[05:05] Roberto Diaz: For the planned benchmark, what exactly will we measure? p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens?
[05:20] Marcus Chen: Exactly, plus sustained throughput over 10min windows, cold-start latency, KV cache hit rates. We'll run with your on-prem corpus to mimic real payloads. I'll share a checklist and the harness.
[05:40] Aisha Khan: A couple of things we've seen: KV cache sometimes shows high miss rates causing spikes. can you explain caching in Redwood?
[05:50] Marcus Chen: Sure. Redwood does prefix and KV caching to reduce repeated compute; occasionally the cache keys change if prompt templates shift which causes miss rates. we also tune chunking and batching. sometimes transcript notes call it 'KV cash' in our internal notes — small transcription quirk.
[06:15] Lena Park: Quick talk about SLA: for Dedicated we can commit to an uptime SLA and p95 latency targets depending on the GPU profile. We don't usually guarantee p99 for free, but committed contracts include escalations and playbooks.
[06:40] Roberto Diaz: That sounds fair. For contract length we're leaning to a 12-month commit to lock pricing. do you offer stepped discounts for higher commits?
[06:50] Lena Park: Yes, we have tiered discounts. For a 12-month committed spend combined with multi-region reserved pools, we can offer incremental discounts. I'll put together a formal quote showing options: 12-month, 24-month, and 12-month + multi-region add-on.
[07:10] Mina Patel: We need that quote formatted for procurement — line items, PO-able, and include SOW for the Dedicated setup.
[07:20] Lena Park: Absolutely.
[07:25] Aisha Khan: One technical question: will quantized models run differently on dedicated infra? cost/perf tradeoffs?
[07:35] Marcus Chen: Yes, quantization and kernel selection matter. Our runtime picks optimized kernels per architecture and sequence length. Quantized weights reduce memory and improve throughput, but there are quality tradeoffs we can measure. Marcus: we'll recommend quant profiles per workload.
[08:00] Roberto Diaz: Any notes about data residency and logs residency for EU region?
[08:10] Lena Park: We can keep logs and metrics in-region for EU dedicated pools; KMS can be region-local. we'll include residency options in the quote.
[08:25] Aisha Khan: Great. Back to benchmarks — timeline to run them? we want results before end of Q1.
[08:35] Marcus Chen: If you can share sample workloads and an S3 bucket access, we can spin up dedicated pools in a staging region and run within 5 business days. we'll need the traffic profile and keys.
[08:50] Aisha Khan: We'll share that by Tuesday.
[09:00] Mina Patel: from procurement, payment terms net30, we'd like an option for net45 as a contingency.
[09:08] Lena Park: We'll note that; final terms usually in PO negotiation.
[09:15] Aisha Khan: Are there any hard limits on autoscaling with dedicated pools? we want burst capacity for marketing spikes.
[09:25] Marcus Chen: We provide burst capacity options — you can configure a policy to allow short-lived burst on shared hosted capacity or reserved crossover. there's a cost for burst usage beyond commit, but you can cap it.
[09:45] Roberto Diaz: Good. any integrations for cost reporting into our observability stack?
[09:52] Lena Park: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards; we can forward reports to Datadog or BigQuery depending on your stack.
[10:10] Aisha Khan: Ok perfect. let's go over the recap now.
[10:15] Lena Park: Recap: SummitCloud wants 2x dedicated capacity, two new regions (eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1), 12-month committed extension, SOC2/KMS/SAML requirements to be validated, run benchmark within 5 business days once payloads provided, procurement to receive PO-able quote. action owners and due dates as noted.
[10:40] Mina Patel: timeline sounds good.
[11:00] Lena Park: Any other questions?
[11:05] Roberto Diaz: none from me.
[11:10] Aisha Khan: no, thanks.
[11:20] Lena Park: Great thanks all. we'll send the quote and benchmark plan. meeting adjourned.
[11:30] --- End of recording (transcription may contain minor errors: product names sometimes auto-changed, e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' appears as 'Redwood Dedi' in a few places).
